Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. A pattern step may be skipped only with a stated reason; one recap per part and one closing recap.
[S2-08] Apply first, name after (Navin, 27 October 2026): in an economics script a concept's real-world example runs BEFORE the beat that names the term: the example beats carry the example's numbers (₹50 → ₹65, buyers 2 → 12 → 3) and walk the mechanism step by step; then the term ('isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain'), then the book's definition, then one line on where the learner meets it in real life. The example is the one Section 1 chose for the item (its place, actors, goods, numbers), economically correct and at the learner's level.

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a write_script card:
- card.parts are this video's parts: each has item ids, one content type and the questions it must answer. The source gives every item's
  full content and its teacher questions with ids ("p003-i4#q2") and answers from BIE's chapter map; teach from them.
- card.coverage.must_cover lists every item this video must teach: each must be in covers_item_ids of a beat that really explains it.
  may_skip lists items you may leave out (not teachable). card.context.map_slice shows the related concepts for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what this video is about, the key questions it must answer, your main decisions (order,
  hook, analogy, where prerequisites are taught) with a reason each, what is uncertain.
- title: the video title in the learner language.
- parts: one entry per card part, with the universal frame of that part (S3-01), each in one or two lines of clear English for BIE:
  process (what happens or what the thing does), how (how it works or happens), when (when, in what order, under which timing),
  conditions (what must be true for it, or what changes it), atmosphere (the setting and situation a student should picture). Write
  "n/a: " and the reason only where a question truly does not apply to that part. skipped_steps = the teaching-pattern steps of this
  part you leave out because there is nothing real to say for them, each with the reason ([] when every step is done); at most half
  of a pattern, never a step that has something real; BIE's code records the reason.
- beats: the whole video in order. beat_id "b1", "b2" ...; part_id = the card part this beat teaches ("" for the opening hook, a
  prerequisite taught first, a transition or the final recap); step = the number of the teaching-pattern step of that part's content type
  that this beat performs (see the content types above; 0 when part_id is "" and for an exam-question part, whose type is "none");
  the steps of a part's pattern appear in order, except the ones skipped with a reason; a classification part follows the family
  pattern: the overview tree first, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape → why it is named so → its special feature
  → its function with its cause → where it is found, by a zoom from the organ → its consequence), then the comparison, then a memory
  trick; one recap per part and one closing recap for the video, never two recaps of the same thing;
  purpose (hook, prerequisite, explain, example, analogy, story, compare, process_walkthrough, misconception, exam_tip,
  question_to_student, recap, transition); say = the exact spoken words, one to four complete spoken sentences in Navin's Hinglish
  (S2-04), the way a teacher speaks to one student, never clipped note-style lines ("Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular." is a teacher's
  beat; "Location: kidney tubules, glandular ducts." is a note):
  mixed script: Hindi words in Devanagari, English words (above all the book's technical terms, spelled as the book spells them) in
  Roman, as in "आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे"; brackets only after a genuinely difficult Hindi word (see "Brackets" below; the
  screen shows the bracket and the voice says "सतह, यानी surface"); never write an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman;
  numbers as digits; addressed to one student; covers_item_ids = the item ids this beat really explains; answers = the teacher question
  ids this beat really answers; on_screen = what the student should see while hearing it (for the director); basis = book, outside or
  mixed.
Opening the book (S2-07; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher, never a reader of the line): every new
topic (every concept and every prerequisite) opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any
book line, the beat carries at least one of: the term opened ("yaani" + its plain meaning + one everyday image), the why from a need or
a problem, or an example or place by a zoom from the organ. The source gives every item's unpack from Section 1 (its terms, why chain,
example, consequence, visual verb) and the locked explanations: speak them, in your own teacher's words, at the depth of the level
profile below. BIE's code sends back a beat whose English words are the book's and that opens nothing ("dohraav pakad"), a clipped
sentence without a verb, a topic that opens without a question, and a second recap of the same thing.
Real-world application (S2-08; Navin, 27 October 2026: "economic concepts ko real world mein apply karke samjhao"): for an economics
definition, cause_effect or process item the source gives the real_world_example Section 1 chose (place, actors, goods, numbers before
→ after, the steps with their mechanism links, the naming sentence, the real-life link). Run that example FIRST, in beats that cover
the item and carry its numbers as digits ("dukaan mein chini ke 3 packet, ₹50 ka ek; kal 2 khareedar, aaj 12"), walking the mechanism
step by step (purpose story or example); only then the beat that names the term ("isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain"), then
the book's definition, then the real-life link. The opening question of such a topic asks about the situation, not the term. BIE's
code sends back a script whose naming beat comes before the example beats, or whose example beats carry none of the numbers.
Time (S2-01): the source gives this video's narration time; BIE's code counts the spoken words (130 a minute) and the script must stay
within it. Win the time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content: every item in must_cover is taught and every
teacher question whose basis is "book" is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the
time allows.
Prerequisites (S2-03): in a topic video they were already taught in the prerequisite video; remind of one in at most 2 beats (purpose
"prerequisite"). In the prerequisite video (card parts "pre1", "pre2" ...) teach each prerequisite simply, with an everyday example, in
the order given: part_id = the prerequisite id, step 0, covers_item_ids = the prerequisite ids the beat teaches, answers [].
A beat introduces at most a few new items: BIE's code measures the load of every beat (0.4 per new item plus 1 per 50 spoken words, at
most 1.8), so a beat holds at most about 70 spoken words with one new item, 50 with two and 30 with three; split longer beats. Reply
with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-27.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.
- Apply it in the real world first, then name it (Navin's sugar shop) (every economics concept (a definition, a cause-and-effect chain, a process): the example runs before the term is named): Ek kirana shop mein chini ke 3 packet hain, ₹50 ka ek. Kal 2 khareedar aaye the, aaj 12 aa gaye; sab ko chini chahiye par packet 3 hi hain. Dukandar daam ₹65 kar deta hai; ab sirf 3 log kharid paate hain, baaki 9 khaali haath. Zyada log, utna hi maal, isliye daam upar. Isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain. Phir book ki definition. Phir: yahi aap Diwali se pehle sabzi mandi mein dekhte hain.

Brackets (word list 2026-10-28.1): use everyday spoken Hindi freely, without brackets (मुख्य, वापस, बराबर, आसपास, इस्तेमाल, करके, जिससे ...). Only a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical) gets its English word in brackets right after it, for example "सतह (surface)", "घर्षण (friction)", "सघन (dense)"; better still, use the book's English term or a simpler Hindi word. Never put a bracket inside an idiom or a fixed phrase: "आम तौर पर", not "आम तौर (usually) पर"; "नहीं के बराबर", not "नहीं के बराबर (equal to)". BIE's code removes a bracket after an everyday word and asks for one only after a Hindi word it does not know as everyday.

Video v10: Bank money, cheque, demand draft और overdraft
Goal: Learner negotiable instruments की पूरी family, promise–order, parties और cheque dishonour समझेगा; prepaid demand draft, credit-based overdraft तथा MICR–IFSC के formats और uses अलग कर सकेगा।
Opening hook: Account में पैसा होना और किसी को cheque देना—क्या दोनों का मतलब payment पूरा हो जाना है?
Story or analogy: एक payment situation में promise करने वाला, order देने वाला और payment पाने वाला अलग दिखेंगे। Family overview के बाद हर instrument को समान criteria पर पढ़ेंगे। Demand draft और overdraft में funding का समय, available credit और इस्तेमाल पर interest अलग होंगे; codes को cheque processing और electronic routing के काम से जोड़ेंगे।
Planned minutes: 10
Narration time (S2-01): 8.1-10.7 minutes, about 1053-1391 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Purchases, prices, debts and payments due later; Bank balances, deposits, loans and interest; Denominations, monetary arithmetic, percentages and minimum–maximum limits; Purchasing power, inflation, scarcity and liquidity; Central bank, commercial bank, government treasury and bank-to-bank settlement; Foreign currencies, exchange rates, reserves and demand–supply changes; Chronological reading: BCE/CE, centuries, dynasties and law versus implementation dates; Digital instructions, identity authentication, ledgers and payment interfaces
Open every book line (S2-07): a question about something the learner can see, then the name; every term opened: its plain meaning with 'yaani' and one everyday image (the word root where it helps); the why, starting from a need or a problem, one link at a time; an example or the place, by a zoom from the organ or the thing the learner knows; the consequence: what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea; the contrast: what it is not, and what the exam confuses it with; the memory beat by level: the exam's 'yaad rakhna', the other names, the trick.

beats.say: Account में पैसे हैं, cheque दे दिया। क्या payment हो गई? पैसा और payment instruction अलग समझो।
beats.on_screen: Balance → instruction → payment?

beats.say: किराना दुकान पर ₹200 भेजे, नोट नहीं दिए। तुम्हारा balance ₹1,000 से ₹800, दुकानदार का ₹500 से ₹700 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Illustration: buyer ₹1,000 → ₹800; seller ₹500 → ₹700

beats.say: इन्हीं balances को bank money या deposit money कहते हैं: bank accounts में जमा पैसा, जिसे banking instruments से transfer करते हो, cash थमाकर नहीं। दुकान पर account payment में यही पैसा इस्तेमाल होता है।
beats.on_screen: Deposit money: account balance transferred without physical cash

beats.say: उधार के माल का written payment claim आगे दे सकते हो? मान लो retailer ने ₹10,000 चुकाने का valid written promise दिया। सही transfer के बाद wholesaler के पास ऐसे documents 1 से 0, supplier के पास 0 से 1 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative valid transfer: ₹10,000 claim; wholesaler 1 → 0, supplier 0 → 1

beats.say: यह negotiable instrument है: transferable written document, जिसमें तय रकम देने का promise या order हो। Negotiable यहाँ payment का हक आगे देना है, bargaining नहीं; ₹10,000 तय रकम है, 'कुछ पैसे' नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Written + specified sum + promise/order + transferable

beats.say: चावल अभी, पैसे बाद में चाहिए तो? मान लो Rahul ने retailer को ₹50,000 का माल उधार दिया; retailer ने 1 January को चुकाने का promise लिखा। उस दिन payment होने पर बकाया ₹50,000 से ₹0 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical rice credit → written promise → settlement

beats.say: यह promissory note है: एक व्यक्ति का दूसरे को तय रकम देने का written promise। Promise करने वाला Maker, Rahul Payee है; 1 January इस example की date है, हर note की नहीं। Business credit में इससे अपनी payment commitment लिखते हो।
beats.on_screen: Maker personally promises → Payee Rahul

beats.say: Wholesaler खुद promise करने के बजाय retailer को लिखे, '₹1 लाख 90 days बाद दो', तो? मान लो credit sale के बाद यह order दिया; 90 days बाद payment पर बकाया ₹1,00,000 से ₹0 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Written order → retailer pays after 90 days → outstanding ₹0

beats.say: यह bill of exchange है: किसी को payment करने का written order। Wholesaler Drawer, retailer Drawee; Payee wholesaler खुद या उसका बताया दूसरा व्यक्ति। Business credit में 3 roles हो सकते हैं, लेकिन जरूरी नहीं कि 3 अलग लोग हों।
beats.on_screen: Drawer orders → Drawee pays → Payee receives; roles may overlap

beats.say: ₹2,000 का किराना लेकर customer bank को दुकानदार के नाम payment लिखे तो? दुकानदार collection के लिए जमा करता है। Successful clearing पर customer का balance ₹10,000 से ₹8,000 और दुकानदार का ₹5,000 से ₹7,000 होता है; केवल कागज़ देने पर नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical groceries ₹2,000 → issue → collection → successful clearing; buyer ₹10,000 → ₹8,000; seller ₹5,000 → ₹7,000

beats.say: यह cheque है: special bill of exchange, drawn on a bank और payable on demand। यानी customer bank से payment करने को कहता है; पेश करने पर payment माँगी जाती है, अलग future maturity का इंतजार नहीं। Supplier या दुकान को ऐसे payment कर सकते हो।
beats.on_screen: Cheque: customer-issued bank order; payable on demand; payment subject to requirements

beats.say: मुँह से promise करना written instrument नहीं। Note में खुद payment मानते हो; bill में दूसरे को payment करने को कहते हो।
beats.on_screen: Boundary: oral assurance ≠ written instrument

beats.say: इन definitions को अब दो सवालों से इस्तेमाल करेंगे: पैसा कहाँ है, और document किसे payment करने को कहता है?
beats.on_screen: Apply definitions: location of money / obligation in document

beats.say: सिर्फ नोट गिनोगे? Modern money supply का सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा bank money है; accounts भी गिनो।
beats.on_screen: Cash is not the whole money supply

beats.say: Document से payment claim का कानूनी सहारा? Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, यानी NIA, transferability और legal enforceability का framework देता है।
beats.on_screen: NIA, 1881 → transfer and enforceable claims

beats.say: बटुए के cash के साथ घर और business के spendable balances रखकर सोचो; तभी modern money का फैलाव समझोगे।
beats.on_screen: Wallet cash alongside household and business deposits

beats.say: 'सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा' कोई fixed percentage नहीं बताता। 1881 को NIA के साल से जोड़ो, money supply के estimate से नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Relative size ≠ fixed percentage; 1881 = Act year

beats.say: Deposits गिनना जरूरी है; payment document में legal enforceability जरूरी है, ताकि शर्तें पूरी होने पर कानून के सहारे रकम माँग सको।
beats.on_screen: Count deposits; enforce payment rights subject to conditions

beats.say: QR, card, कागज़—एक family? Channels हैं cheques, UPI, debit cards, NEFT, RTGS और दूसरे रास्ते; legal instruments हैं promissory note, bill of exchange, cheque।
beats.on_screen: Two trees: channels / three negotiable instruments

beats.say: QR से UPI, Unified Payments Interface, पर instant account payment; debit card से linked balance इस्तेमाल; cheque से bank को written order।
beats.on_screen: App / card / written instruction

beats.say: NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer, में batches; RTGS, Real Time Gross Settlement, में हर transfer अलग, पूरी amount का real-time settlement। दोनों में beneficiary details देते हो।
beats.on_screen: NEFT: batches | RTGS: individual gross settlement

beats.say: इन 2 cards की wording देखो: Rahul वाले में 'I promise to pay', इसलिए Promissory Note; retailer वाले में payment का order, इसलिए Bill of Exchange। पहले में खुद की commitment, दूसरे में दूसरे को direction है।
beats.on_screen: Same criteria: written form / obligation / who must pay / credit use

beats.say: तीसरे card में grocery customer का order bank को गया था। इसलिए Cheque bank पर drawn bill है; bank ने customer का order लिखा नहीं, उसे payment करने को कहा गया है।
beats.on_screen: Same criteria: written order / customer issues / bank pays / grocery purchase

beats.say: एक ही criterion लगाओ: payment की बात किससे जुड़ी है? Note के Maker से, bill के Drawee से, cheque के bank से। UPI channel है, इस 3-instrument list का चौथा member नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Side-by-side: own promise / another party ordered / bank ordered

beats.say: याद रखो: 'मैं दूँगा', 'तुम दो', 'bank दे'। Channel बदलने से deposit अलग किस्म का पैसा नहीं बनता।
beats.on_screen: Three-part memory cue; money ≠ channel

beats.say: उसी grocery payment में customer, bank और दुकानदार कहाँ बैठते हैं? अब 3 roles का रास्ता देखो।
beats.on_screen: Reuse the ₹2,000 grocery transaction

beats.say: Customer Drawer है; order उसके bank, यानी Drawee को गया; दुकानदार Payee है।
beats.on_screen: Customer: Drawer → bank: Drawee → shopkeeper: Payee

beats.say: Drawer की पहचान लिखने से है, Drawee की order पाने से; Payee वह है जिसे रकम मिलनी है।
beats.on_screen: Role functions attached to the same three actors

beats.say: Collection और successful clearing इन roles को जोड़ते हैं; तभी दोनों balances बदलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Collection → successful clearing → both balance changes

beats.say: इस labelled रास्ते में customer का order और दुकानदार को payment अलग arrows हैं।
beats.on_screen: Labelled recap: instruction arrow versus payment arrow

beats.say: ₹2,000 का cheque, balance ₹500—क्या होगा? मान लो bank ने लौटाया; returned cheques इस transaction में 0 से 1 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Insufficient funds → returned unpaid

beats.say: Drawer को statutory demand notice, यानी कानून के मुताबिक पैसे माँगता notice मिला; फिर भी नहीं चुकाया। यह cheque dishonour का Section 138 वाला क्रम है।
beats.on_screen: Notice received → continued non-payment

beats.say: ₹500 से ₹2,000 नहीं चुकते, इसलिए cheque लौटा: यह dishonour है। Notice के बाद भी unpaid रहे तो Section 138 की criminal liability, statutory conditions के साथ।
beats.on_screen: ₹500 < ₹2,000 → return → notice → unpaid; statutory conditions apply

beats.say: हर returned cheque automatic crime नहीं। पूरी statutory conditions जाँचनी होंगी; केवल return देखकर फैसला मत करना।
beats.on_screen: Return alone ≠ automatic offence

beats.say: पूरा क्रम देखो: रकम कम, cheque वापस, notice के बाद भी payment नहीं, फिर statutory conditions की जाँच।
beats.on_screen: Insufficient funds → return → notice → unpaid → legal conditions

beats.say: Section 138 में return अकेला पूरा legal test नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Return alone ≠ complete legal test

beats.say: Fee भेजने से पहले bank को ₹5,000 दो तो? Charges छोड़कर funding ₹0 से ₹5,000 हुई; फिर institution के लिए instrument निकला।
beats.on_screen: Fund first → issue fee instrument

beats.say: अपने ₹10,000, supplier को ₹15,000 चाहिए तो? Approved facility ने extra ₹5,000 दिए; borrowing ₹0 से ₹5,000 हुई।
beats.on_screen: Own ₹10,000 + approved credit ₹5,000

beats.say: पहला Demand Draft है: secure transfer का bank-issued prepaid instrument। Recharge जैसे पहले पैसे; ordinary cheque में बाद में account से payment माँगते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Demand draft: prepaid, bank-issued

beats.say: दूसरा Overdraft है: short-term credit से अपने balance से ज्यादा निकालना। Supplier के extra ₹5,000 लौटाने होंगे, savings नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Temporary gap → borrowed excess → repayment obligation

beats.say: Draft borrowing नहीं। खाली account अपने आप OD permission नहीं देता; उसके लिए approved credit facility चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Prepaid ≠ credit; OD requires approval

beats.say: Fee draft में advance funding; temporary business gap में OD borrowing।
beats.on_screen: Prepaid fee transfer / short-term business credit

beats.say: Recipient बाद के balance पर क्यों निर्भर नहीं? Customer ने पहले ₹3,000 दिए; backing ₹0 से ₹3,000 हुई, फिर draft निकला।
beats.on_screen: Receive ₹3,000 → issue ₹3,000 draft

beats.say: इसी prepayment से bank guarantee आती है: bank के पास payment की backing पहले पहुँच चुकी है।
beats.on_screen: Cause: funds already received

beats.say: इसलिए draft की रकम के लिए customer के later account balance पर भरोसा नहीं करना पड़ता।
beats.on_screen: Pre-funding removes reliance on later customer balance

beats.say: ₹3,000 की backing और ₹3,000 का draft साथ मिलाकर देखो; funding गायब नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Match received funds ₹3,000 with draft ₹3,000

beats.say: यह funding की सुरक्षा है, हर तरह की payment problem खत्म होने का दावा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Limit: funding assurance, not immunity from every problem

beats.say: Guarantee की वजह याद रखो: पहले मिली रकम।
beats.on_screen: Advance funding → bank guarantee

beats.say: अपने ₹10,000 और OD Limit ₹40,000 हो तो कितना उपलब्ध? चित्र own funds और credit अलग करके जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: OD illustration: own funds plus credit

beats.say: बाएँ ₹10,000 अपने; दाएँ ₹40,000 borrowing ceiling। अलग डिब्बों जैसे समझो; arrow अपने पैसे को loan नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Separate boxes: own ₹10,000 / approved credit up to ₹40,000

beats.say: कुल ₹10,000 plus ₹40,000, यानी up to ₹50,000। Maximum है, निकालना जरूरी नहीं; interest केवल इस्तेमाल हुई OD पर।
beats.on_screen: Maximum ₹50,000; interest on used credit only

beats.say: ₹25,000 निकाले: ₹10,000 अपने, ₹15,000 borrowed। Interest principal ₹15,000 है; calculation के लिए rate और समय भी चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Shade only ₹15,000 used OD

beats.say: ₹50,000 availability, इस्तेमाल हुई credit debt है। ₹40,000 OD सबका हक नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustration, not universal entitlement; availability ≠ utilisation

beats.say: Jan Dhan account से automatic OD? Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana में eligible account holders को facility मिल सकती है।
beats.on_screen: PMJDY → eligible holders → possible OD

beats.say: 'Eligible' और 'may receive' पर ध्यान दो: तय शर्तें पूरी करने पर credit मिल सकता है; account खुलना अपने आप borrowing की मंजूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Account access ≠ automatic credit eligibility

beats.say: Exam में 'हर holder को automatic OD' से बचो; access conditional है।
beats.on_screen: Conditional, not automatic

beats.say: Cheque का machine-readable code कैसा? MICR, Magnetic Ink Character Recognition: 9 digits, Iron Oxide ink, automated clearance के लिए।
beats.on_screen: MICR: 9 digits; magnetic ink; cheque clearance

beats.say: ₹2,000 भेजने के form में कौन-सी branch चुनी जाए? सही 11-character branch code और account details भरने पर identified destination branches 0 से 1 हुईं।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative ₹2,000 transfer: unidentified branch → one identified branch

beats.say: यह Indian Financial System Code, IFSC है: electronic payment systems में participating bank branch का unique 11-character alphanumeric code। यानी letters और numbers वाला branch address, 11 digits नहीं।
beats.on_screen: IFSC: unique branch identifier; 11 alphanumeric characters

beats.say: यह individual account number नहीं; building का पता और कमरे का नंबर अलग होने जैसे branch और account अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: Branch address ≠ individual account identifier

beats.say: Transfer form में IFSC branch पहचानता है; अब इसके payment uses को MICR से अलग रखो।
beats.on_screen: Apply IFSC to electronic transfer routing

beats.say: 100 cheques कैसे पढ़ोगे? मान लो machine processing से pending batch 100 से 0 हुआ; speed का दावा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative pending batch: 100 → 0; no measured speed

beats.say: यह MICR-enabled processing है। Ink की magnetic properties से suitable machine characters पहचानती है; ink सजावट नहीं, पढ़ने में मदद है।
beats.on_screen: Magnetic properties → character recognition

beats.say: जैसे files अलग खानों में रखो, machine cheques sort करती है। Manual reading घटती है, processing जल्दी और accurate होती है।
beats.on_screen: Readable characters → consistent sorting → faster, accurate processing

beats.say: इस batch में 100 pending cheques process हुए; इससे machine handling का काम समझो, measured speed नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative completed batch, not a speed benchmark

beats.say: बेहतर accuracy का मतलब zero errors नहीं; machine readability fixed processing speed की guarantee भी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Improved accuracy ≠ error-free; no fixed-speed guarantee

beats.say: MICR की chain है: readable characters से sorting और processing आसान।
beats.on_screen: Recognition → sorting → processing

beats.say: Electronic transfer में branch routing के लिए IFSC NEFT, RTGS और account-number-based IMPS में इस्तेमाल होता है। IMPS, यानी Immediate Payment Service, तुरंत transfer देता है; इसके दूसरे addressing modes भी हैं।
beats.on_screen: IFSC uses: NEFT / RTGS / account-based IMPS; alternative IMPS addressing exists

beats.say: Format साथ रखो: MICR के 9 digits और magnetic ink cheque clearance के लिए; IFSC के 11 alphanumeric characters electronic branch identification के लिए। दोनों को account number मत समझना।
beats.on_screen: MICR: 9 digits, cheque processing | IFSC: 11 characters, branch routing

beats.say: 9 और 11 code lengths हैं, payment speeds नहीं। NEFT का batch settlement, RTGS का individual settlement और IMPS का instant transfer अलग बातें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Code length ≠ speed; distinguish identification from transfer mechanism

beats.say: Exam में format और function मिलाओ: cheque processing या electronic branch routing। सही branch के साथ सही beneficiary account details भी चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Match code to function; branch routing alone does not identify the recipient account

beats.say: अब शुरुआत का जवाब: cheque देना instruction है; successful payment अलग stage है। Payment समझते समय पैसा, order, funding और destination—ये 4 चीजें अलग जाँचो।
beats.on_screen: Final checklist: money / instruction / funding / destination

replace_beats.on_screen: Maker personally promises → Payee Rahul

replace_beats.say: Wholesaler retailer को लिखे, '₹1 लाख 90 days बाद दो', तो? मान लो credit sale का यह order पूरा हुआ; 90 days बाद payment से बकाया ₹1,00,000 से ₹0 हुआ।
replace_beats.on_screen: Written order → retailer pays after 90 days → outstanding ₹0

replace_beats.on_screen: Customer-issued bank order; payment on presentation subject to requirements

replace_beats.say: 'कल दे दूँगा' सिर्फ बोलना document नहीं। Note में खुद देने का वादा; bill में दूसरे से कहते हो, 'इसे पैसे दो'।
replace_beats.on_screen: Oral assurance ≠ written instrument; own undertaking versus direction to another

replace_beats.say: अब पूछो: पैसा कहाँ है, और document किसे payment करने को कहता है?
replace_beats.on_screen: Apply definitions: money location / payment obligation

replace_beats.say: बटुए के cash के साथ घर और business के spendable balances भी गिनो।
replace_beats.on_screen: Wallet cash alongside household and business deposits

replace_beats.say: यह relative claim है, percentage या dated estimate नहीं; 1881 Act का साल है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Relative size; no percentage/date estimate; 1881 = Act year

replace_beats.say: Deposits भी पैसा हैं; enforceability यानी शर्तें पूरी हों तो कानून से payment माँग सको।
replace_beats.on_screen: Count deposits; legally supported payment claims

replace_beats.say: Rahul वाले card में 'I promise to pay': Promissory Note, अपनी commitment। Retailer को payment का order: Bill of Exchange, दूसरे को direction। दोनों business credit के written documents हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Written form / own promise versus order / obligated party / credit use

replace_beats.say: Grocery customer का order bank को गया: Cheque bank पर drawn bill है। Customer लिखता है, bank को payment करने का निर्देश मिलता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Written order / customer issues / bank pays / grocery purchase

replace_beats.say: किसे payment करनी है? Note में Maker, bill में Drawee, cheque में bank। UPI channel है, इस legal family का चौथा member नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Own promise / another party ordered / bank ordered; UPI is a channel

replace_beats.say: Grocery payment में customer, bank, दुकानदार के roles कहाँ हैं?
replace_beats.on_screen: Reuse the ₹2,000 grocery transaction

replace_beats.say: लिखने वाला Drawer, निर्देश पाने वाला Drawee, रकम पाने वाला Payee है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Writer / instructed bank / recipient

replace_beats.say: Collection के बाद successful clearing इन roles को जोड़कर balances बदलती है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Collection → successful clearing → balance changes

replace_beats.say: Labels देखो: customer का order और दुकानदार को payment अलग arrows हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Labelled instruction and payment arrows

replace_beats.say: रकम कम, इसलिए unpaid return यानी dishonour। Notice के बाद भी payment नहीं: statutory conditions पूरी हों तो Section 138 में criminal offence।
replace_beats.on_screen: Insufficient funds → return → notice → unpaid; statutory conditions apply

replace_beats.say: हर return automatic crime नहीं; पूरी statutory conditions जाँचनी होंगी।
replace_beats.on_screen: Return alone ≠ automatic offence

replace_beats.say: क्रम देखो: रकम कम, return, notice, फिर भी unpaid, फिर कानूनी शर्तों की जाँच।
replace_beats.on_screen: Funds short → return → notice → unpaid → statutory conditions

replace_beats.say: Draft borrowing नहीं; खाली account OD permission नहीं। Approved credit चाहिए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Prepaid ≠ credit; OD requires approval

replace_beats.say: इसलिए customer के later balance से draft funding जुटाने की जरूरत नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: No reliance on later customer balance for draft funding

replace_beats.say: Backing ₹3,000, draft ₹3,000: दोनों रकम मिलाकर जाँचो।
replace_beats.on_screen: Received ₹3,000 matches draft ₹3,000

replace_beats.say: यह funding assurance है, हर payment problem मिटने की guarantee नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Funding assurance ≠ immunity from every problem

replace_beats.say: Availability और debt अलग हैं; यह ₹40,000 limit सबका हक नहीं।

replace_beats.say: Branch और account अलग हैं, जैसे building का पता और कमरे का नंबर।
replace_beats.on_screen: Branch identifier ≠ account number

replace_beats.say: Form में IFSC branch पहचानता है, account नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Apply IFSC: electronic destination branch

replace_beats.on_screen: Illustrative completion, not a speed benchmark

beats.say: चावल अभी, पैसे बाद में चाहिए तो? मान लो Rahul ने retailer को ₹50,000 का माल उधार दिया; retailer ने 1 January को चुकाने का promise लिखा। उस दिन payment होने पर बकाया ₹50,000 से ₹0 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical rice credit → written promise → settlement

beats.say: यह promissory note है: दूसरे को तय रकम देने का written promise। Promise करने वाला Maker, Rahul Payee है; 1 January सिर्फ इस example की date है। Business credit में अपनी commitment ऐसे लिखते हो।
beats.on_screen: Maker personally promises → Payee Rahul

beats.say: Wholesaler retailer को लिखे, '₹1 लाख 90 days बाद दो', तो? मान लो credit sale का यह order पूरा हुआ; 90 days बाद payment से बकाया ₹1,00,000 से ₹0 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Written order → retailer pays after 90 days → outstanding ₹0

beats.say: यह bill of exchange है: दूसरे को payment का written order। Wholesaler Drawer, retailer Drawee; Payee wholesaler या उसका बताया व्यक्ति। इसलिए 3 roles का मतलब 3 अलग लोग जरूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Drawer orders → Drawee pays → Payee receives; roles may overlap

beats.say: ₹2,000 का किराना लेकर customer bank को दुकानदार के नाम payment लिखे तो? दुकानदार collection के लिए जमा करता है। Successful clearing पर customer का balance ₹10,000 से ₹8,000 और दुकानदार का ₹5,000 से ₹7,000 होता है; केवल कागज़ देने पर नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical groceries ₹2,000 → issue → collection → successful clearing; buyer ₹10,000 → ₹8,000; seller ₹5,000 → ₹7,000

beats.say: यह cheque है: special bill of exchange, drawn on a bank और payable on demand। यानी bank को payment का निर्देश; पेश करके payment माँगो, अलग future maturity का इंतजार नहीं। Supplier payment में इसका इस्तेमाल होता है।
beats.on_screen: Customer-issued bank order; payment on presentation subject to requirements

beats.say: 'कल दे दूँगा' सिर्फ बोलना document नहीं। Note में खुद देने का वादा; bill में दूसरे से कहते हो, 'इसे पैसे दो'।
beats.on_screen: Oral assurance ≠ written instrument; own undertaking versus direction to another

beats.say: अब पूछो: पैसा कहाँ है, और document किसे payment करने को कहता है?
beats.on_screen: Apply definitions: money location / payment obligation

beats.say: सिर्फ नोट गिनोगे? Modern money supply का सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा bank money है; accounts भी गिनो।
beats.on_screen: Cash is not the whole money supply

beats.say: Document से payment claim का कानूनी सहारा? Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, यानी NIA, transferability और legal enforceability का framework देता है।
beats.on_screen: NIA, 1881 → transfer and enforceable claims

beats.say: बटुए के cash के साथ घर और business के spendable balances भी गिनो।
beats.on_screen: Wallet cash alongside household and business deposits

beats.say: यह relative claim है, percentage या dated estimate नहीं; 1881 Act का साल है।
beats.on_screen: Relative size; no percentage/date estimate; 1881 = Act year

beats.say: Deposits भी पैसा हैं; enforceability यानी शर्तें पूरी हों तो कानून से payment माँग सको।
beats.on_screen: Count deposits; legally supported payment claims

beats.say: QR, card, कागज़—एक family? Channels हैं cheques, UPI, debit cards, NEFT, RTGS और दूसरे रास्ते; legal instruments हैं promissory note, bill of exchange, cheque।
beats.on_screen: Two trees: channels / three negotiable instruments

beats.say: QR से UPI, Unified Payments Interface, पर instant account payment; debit card से linked balance इस्तेमाल; cheque से bank को written order।
beats.on_screen: App / card / written instruction

beats.say: NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer, में batches; RTGS, Real Time Gross Settlement, में हर transfer अलग, पूरी amount का real-time settlement। दोनों में beneficiary details देते हो।
beats.on_screen: NEFT: batches | RTGS: individual gross settlement

beats.say: Rahul वाले card में 'I promise to pay': Promissory Note, अपनी commitment। Retailer को payment का order: Bill of Exchange, दूसरे को direction। दोनों business credit के written documents हैं।
beats.on_screen: Written form / own promise versus order / obligated party / credit use

beats.say: Grocery customer का order bank को गया: Cheque bank पर drawn bill है। Customer लिखता है, bank को payment करने का निर्देश मिलता है।
beats.on_screen: Written order / customer issues / bank pays / grocery purchase

beats.say: किसे payment करनी है? Note में Maker, bill में Drawee, cheque में bank। UPI channel है, इस legal family का चौथा member नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Own promise / another party ordered / bank ordered; UPI is a channel

beats.say: याद रखो: 'मैं दूँगा', 'तुम दो', 'bank दे'। Channel बदलने से deposit अलग किस्म का पैसा नहीं बनता।
beats.on_screen: Three-part memory cue; money ≠ channel

beats.say: Grocery payment में customer, bank, दुकानदार के roles कहाँ हैं?
beats.on_screen: Reuse the ₹2,000 grocery transaction

beats.say: Customer Drawer है; order उसके bank, यानी Drawee को गया; दुकानदार Payee है।
beats.on_screen: Customer: Drawer → bank: Drawee → shopkeeper: Payee

beats.say: लिखने वाला Drawer, निर्देश पाने वाला Drawee, रकम पाने वाला Payee है।
beats.on_screen: Writer / instructed bank / recipient

beats.say: Collection के बाद successful clearing इन roles को जोड़कर balances बदलती है।
beats.on_screen: Collection → successful clearing → balance changes

beats.say: Labels देखो: customer का order और दुकानदार को payment अलग arrows हैं।
beats.on_screen: Labelled instruction and payment arrows

beats.say: ₹2,000 का cheque, balance ₹500—क्या होगा? मान लो bank ने लौटाया; returned cheques इस transaction में 0 से 1 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Insufficient funds → returned unpaid

beats.say: Drawer को statutory demand notice, यानी कानून के मुताबिक पैसे माँगता notice मिला; फिर भी नहीं चुकाया। यह cheque dishonour का Section 138 वाला क्रम है।
beats.on_screen: Notice received → continued non-payment

beats.say: रकम कम, इसलिए unpaid return यानी dishonour। Notice के बाद भी payment नहीं: statutory conditions पूरी हों तो Section 138 में criminal offence।
beats.on_screen: Insufficient funds → return → notice → unpaid; statutory conditions apply

beats.say: हर return automatic crime नहीं; पूरी statutory conditions जाँचनी होंगी।
beats.on_screen: Return alone ≠ automatic offence

beats.say: क्रम देखो: रकम कम, return, notice, फिर भी unpaid, फिर कानूनी शर्तों की जाँच।
beats.on_screen: Funds short → return → notice → unpaid → statutory conditions

beats.say: Section 138 में return अकेला पूरा legal test नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Return alone ≠ complete legal test

beats.say: Fee भेजने से पहले bank को ₹5,000 दो तो? Charges छोड़कर funding ₹0 से ₹5,000 हुई; फिर institution के लिए instrument निकला।
beats.on_screen: Fund first → issue fee instrument

beats.say: अपने ₹10,000, supplier को ₹15,000 चाहिए तो? Approved facility ने extra ₹5,000 दिए; borrowing ₹0 से ₹5,000 हुई।
beats.on_screen: Own ₹10,000 + approved credit ₹5,000

beats.say: पहला Demand Draft है: secure transfer का bank-issued prepaid instrument। Recharge जैसे पहले पैसे; ordinary cheque में बाद में account से payment माँगते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Demand draft: prepaid, bank-issued

beats.say: दूसरा Overdraft है: short-term credit से अपने balance से ज्यादा निकालना। Supplier के extra ₹5,000 लौटाने होंगे, savings नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Temporary gap → borrowed excess → repayment obligation

beats.say: Draft borrowing नहीं; खाली account OD permission नहीं। Approved credit चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Prepaid ≠ credit; OD requires approval

beats.say: Fee draft में advance funding; temporary business gap में OD borrowing।
beats.on_screen: Prepaid fee transfer / short-term business credit

beats.say: Recipient बाद के balance पर क्यों निर्भर नहीं? Customer ने पहले ₹3,000 दिए; backing ₹0 से ₹3,000 हुई, फिर draft निकला।
beats.on_screen: Receive ₹3,000 → issue ₹3,000 draft

beats.say: इसी prepayment से bank guarantee आती है: bank के पास payment की backing पहले पहुँच चुकी है।
beats.on_screen: Cause: funds already received

beats.say: इसलिए customer के later balance से draft funding जुटाने की जरूरत नहीं।
beats.on_screen: No reliance on later customer balance for draft funding

beats.say: Backing ₹3,000, draft ₹3,000: दोनों रकम मिलाकर जाँचो।
beats.on_screen: Received ₹3,000 matches draft ₹3,000

beats.say: यह funding assurance है, हर payment problem मिटने की guarantee नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Funding assurance ≠ immunity from every problem

beats.say: Guarantee की वजह याद रखो: पहले मिली रकम।
beats.on_screen: Advance funding → bank guarantee

beats.say: अपने ₹10,000 और OD Limit ₹40,000 हो तो कितना उपलब्ध? चित्र own funds और credit अलग करके जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: OD illustration: own funds plus credit

beats.say: बाएँ ₹10,000 अपने; दाएँ ₹40,000 borrowing ceiling। अलग डिब्बों जैसे समझो; arrow अपने पैसे को loan नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Separate boxes: own ₹10,000 / approved credit up to ₹40,000

beats.say: कुल ₹10,000 plus ₹40,000, यानी up to ₹50,000। Maximum है, निकालना जरूरी नहीं; interest केवल इस्तेमाल हुई OD पर।
beats.on_screen: Maximum ₹50,000; interest on used credit only

beats.say: ₹25,000 निकाले: ₹10,000 अपने, ₹15,000 borrowed। Interest principal ₹15,000 है; calculation के लिए rate और समय भी चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Shade only ₹15,000 used OD

beats.say: Availability और debt अलग हैं; यह ₹40,000 limit सबका हक नहीं।
beats.on_screen: ₹10,000 + ₹40,000 = ₹50,000 availability; only used OD is debt; illustrative limit

beats.say: Jan Dhan account से automatic OD? Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana में eligible account holders को facility मिल सकती है।
beats.on_screen: PMJDY → eligible holders → possible OD

beats.say: 'Eligible', 'may receive': शर्तें पूरी हों तो credit मिल सकता है; account खुलना borrowing की मंजूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Account access ≠ automatic credit eligibility

beats.say: Exam में 'हर holder को automatic OD' से बचो; access conditional है।
beats.on_screen: Conditional, not automatic

beats.say: Cheque का machine-readable code कैसा? MICR, Magnetic Ink Character Recognition: 9 digits, Iron Oxide ink, automated clearance के लिए।
beats.on_screen: MICR: 9 digits; magnetic ink; cheque clearance

beats.say: ₹2,000 transfer किस branch को जाए? सही 11-character code और account details भरे; identified destination branches 0 से 1 हुईं।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative transfer: unidentified branch → one identified branch

beats.say: यह Indian Financial System Code, IFSC है: electronic payment systems में participating bank branch का unique 11-character alphanumeric code। यानी letters और numbers वाला branch address, 11 digits नहीं।
beats.on_screen: IFSC: unique branch identifier; 11 alphanumeric characters

beats.say: Branch और account अलग हैं, जैसे building का पता और कमरे का नंबर।
beats.on_screen: Branch identifier ≠ account number

beats.say: Form में IFSC branch पहचानता है, account नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Apply IFSC: electronic destination branch

beats.say: 100 cheques कैसे पढ़ोगे? मान लो machine processing से pending batch 100 से 0 हुआ; speed का दावा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative pending batch: 100 → 0; no measured speed

beats.say: यह MICR-enabled processing है। Ink की magnetic properties से suitable machine characters पहचानती है; ink सजावट नहीं, पढ़ने में मदद है।
beats.on_screen: Magnetic properties → character recognition

beats.say: जैसे files अलग खानों में रखो, machine cheques sort करती है। Manual reading घटती है, processing जल्दी और accurate होती है।
beats.on_screen: Readable characters → consistent sorting → faster, accurate processing

beats.say: Pending 100 से 0: यह completed batch है, measured speed नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative completion, not a speed benchmark

beats.say: बेहतर accuracy का मतलब zero errors या fixed speed नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Improvement ≠ error-free processing or fixed speed

beats.say: MICR की chain है: readable characters से sorting और processing आसान।
beats.on_screen: Recognition → sorting → processing

beats.say: Electronic transfer में branch routing के लिए IFSC NEFT, RTGS और account-number-based IMPS में इस्तेमाल होता है। IMPS, यानी Immediate Payment Service, तुरंत transfer देता है; इसके दूसरे addressing modes भी हैं।
beats.on_screen: IFSC uses: NEFT / RTGS / account-based IMPS; alternative IMPS addressing exists

beats.say: साथ देखो: MICR के 9 digits, magnetic ink से cheque clearance; IFSC के 11 alphanumeric characters से electronic branch पहचान। Account number अलग है।
beats.on_screen: MICR: 9 digits, cheque processing | IFSC: 11 characters, branch routing

beats.say: ये code lengths हैं, speeds नहीं: NEFT batches, RTGS individual settlement, IMPS instant transfer देता है।
beats.on_screen: Code format versus payment mechanism

beats.say: Exam में format से function मिलाओ; सही branch के साथ सही beneficiary account भी चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Match code and function; correct branch + correct account

beats.say: अब शुरुआत का जवाब: cheque देना instruction है; successful payment अलग stage है। Payment समझते समय पैसा, order, funding और destination—ये 4 चीजें अलग जाँचो।
beats.on_screen: Final checklist: money / instruction / funding / destination

beats.say: Account में पैसे हैं, cheque दे दिया। क्या payment हो गई? पैसा और payment instruction अलग समझो।
beats.on_screen: Balance → instruction → payment?

beats.say: किराना दुकान पर ₹200 भेजे, नोट नहीं दिए। तुम्हारा balance ₹1,000 से ₹800, दुकानदार का ₹500 से ₹700 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Illustration: buyer ₹1,000 → ₹800; seller ₹500 → ₹700

beats.say: इन्हीं balances को bank money या deposit money कहते हैं: bank accounts में जमा पैसा, जिसे banking instruments से transfer करते हो, cash थमाकर नहीं। दुकान पर account payment में यही पैसा इस्तेमाल होता है।
beats.on_screen: Deposit money: account balance transferred without physical cash

beats.say: उधार का written claim आगे दे सकते हो? Retailer का ₹10,000 का valid promise सही तरह transfer हुआ: wholesaler के documents 1 से 0, supplier के 0 से 1 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative valid transfer: ₹10,000 claim; wholesaler 1 → 0, supplier 0 → 1

beats.say: यह negotiable instrument है: transferable written document में तय रकम का promise या order। Negotiable यानी payment का हक आगे देना, bargaining नहीं; ₹10,000, न कि 'कुछ पैसे'।
beats.on_screen: Written + specified sum + promise/order + transferable

beats.say: चावल अभी, पैसे बाद में चाहिए तो? मान लो Rahul ने retailer को ₹50,000 का माल उधार दिया; retailer ने 1 January को चुकाने का promise लिखा। उस दिन payment होने पर बकाया ₹50,000 से ₹0 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical rice credit → written promise → settlement

beats.say: यह promissory note है: दूसरे को तय रकम देने का written promise। Promise करने वाला Maker, Rahul Payee है; 1 January सिर्फ इस example की date है। Business credit में अपनी commitment ऐसे लिखते हो।
beats.on_screen: Maker personally promises → Payee Rahul

beats.say: Wholesaler retailer को लिखे, '₹1 लाख 90 days बाद दो', तो? मान लो credit sale का यह order पूरा हुआ; 90 days बाद payment से बकाया ₹1,00,000 से ₹0 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Written order → retailer pays after 90 days → outstanding ₹0

beats.say: यह bill of exchange है: दूसरे को payment का written order। Wholesaler Drawer, retailer Drawee; Payee wholesaler या उसका बताया व्यक्ति। इसलिए 3 roles का मतलब 3 अलग लोग जरूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Drawer orders → Drawee pays → Payee receives; roles may overlap

beats.say: ₹2,000 का किराना लेकर customer bank को दुकानदार के नाम payment लिखे तो? दुकानदार collection के लिए जमा करता है। Successful clearing पर customer का balance ₹10,000 से ₹8,000 और दुकानदार का ₹5,000 से ₹7,000 होता है; केवल कागज़ देने पर नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical groceries ₹2,000 → issue → collection → successful clearing; buyer ₹10,000 → ₹8,000; seller ₹5,000 → ₹7,000

beats.say: यह cheque है: special bill of exchange, drawn on a bank और payable on demand। यानी bank को payment instruction; पेश करके payment माँगो, अलग future maturity का इंतजार नहीं। Supplier payment में इसका इस्तेमाल होता है।
beats.on_screen: Customer-issued bank order; payment on presentation subject to requirements

beats.say: 'कल दे दूँगा' सिर्फ बोलना document नहीं। Note में खुद देने का वादा; bill में दूसरे से कहते हो, 'इसे पैसे दो'।
beats.on_screen: Oral assurance ≠ written instrument; own undertaking versus direction to another

beats.say: अब पूछो: पैसा कहाँ है, और document किसे payment करने को कहता है?
beats.on_screen: Apply definitions: money location / payment obligation

beats.say: सिर्फ नोट गिनोगे? Modern money supply का सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा bank money है; accounts भी गिनो।
beats.on_screen: Cash is not the whole money supply

beats.say: Document से payment claim का कानूनी सहारा? Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, यानी NIA, transferability और legal enforceability का framework देता है।
beats.on_screen: NIA, 1881 → transfer and enforceable claims

beats.say: बटुए के cash के साथ घर और business के spendable balances भी गिनो।
beats.on_screen: Wallet cash alongside household and business deposits

beats.say: यह relative claim है, percentage या dated estimate नहीं; 1881 Act का साल है।
beats.on_screen: Relative size; no percentage/date estimate; 1881 = Act year

beats.say: Deposits भी पैसा हैं; enforceability यानी शर्तें पूरी हों तो कानून से payment माँग सको।
beats.on_screen: Count deposits; legally supported payment claims

beats.say: QR, card, कागज़—एक family? Channels हैं cheques, UPI, debit cards, NEFT, RTGS और दूसरे रास्ते; legal instruments हैं promissory note, bill of exchange, cheque।
beats.on_screen: Two trees: channels / three negotiable instruments

beats.say: QR से UPI, Unified Payments Interface, पर instant account payment; debit card से linked balance इस्तेमाल; cheque से bank को written order।
beats.on_screen: App / card / written instruction

beats.say: NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer, में batches; RTGS, Real Time Gross Settlement, में हर transfer अलग, पूरी amount का real-time settlement। दोनों में beneficiary details देते हो।
beats.on_screen: NEFT: batches | RTGS: individual gross settlement

beats.say: Rahul वाले card में 'I promise to pay': Promissory Note, अपनी commitment। Retailer को payment का order: Bill of Exchange, दूसरे को direction। दोनों business credit के written documents हैं।
beats.on_screen: Written form / own promise versus order / obligated party / credit use

beats.say: Cash नहीं देना, इसलिए customer bank से दुकानदार को चुकाने को कहता है। Cheque में drawn on a bank यानी instruction bank को, लिखता customer है।
beats.on_screen: Customer writes the cheque → instruction addressed to bank → shopkeeper receives payment after successful processing

beats.say: किसे payment करनी है? Note में Maker, bill में Drawee, cheque में bank। UPI channel है, इस legal family का चौथा member नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Own promise / another party ordered / bank ordered; UPI is a channel

beats.say: याद रखो: 'मैं दूँगा', 'तुम दो', 'bank दे'। Channel बदलने से deposit अलग किस्म का पैसा नहीं बनता।
beats.on_screen: Three-part memory cue; money ≠ channel

beats.say: Grocery payment में customer, bank, दुकानदार के roles कहाँ हैं?
beats.on_screen: Reuse the ₹2,000 grocery transaction

beats.say: Customer Drawer है; order उसके bank, यानी Drawee को गया; दुकानदार Payee है।
beats.on_screen: Customer: Drawer → bank: Drawee → shopkeeper: Payee

beats.say: लिखने वाला Drawer, instruction पाने वाला Drawee, रकम पाने वाला Payee है।
beats.on_screen: Writer / instructed bank / recipient

beats.say: Collection के बाद successful clearing इन roles को जोड़कर balances बदलती है।
beats.on_screen: Collection → successful clearing → balance changes

beats.say: Labels देखो: customer का order और दुकानदार को payment अलग arrows हैं।
beats.on_screen: Labelled instruction and payment arrows

beats.say: ₹2,000 का cheque, balance ₹500—क्या होगा? मान लो bank ने लौटाया; returned cheques इस transaction में 0 से 1 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Insufficient funds → returned unpaid

beats.say: Drawer को statutory demand notice, यानी कानून के मुताबिक पैसे माँगता notice मिला; फिर भी नहीं चुकाया। यह cheque dishonour का Section 138 वाला क्रम है।
beats.on_screen: Notice received → continued non-payment

beats.say: रकम कम, इसलिए unpaid return यानी dishonour। Notice के बाद भी payment नहीं: statutory conditions पूरी हों तो Section 138 में criminal offence।
beats.on_screen: Insufficient funds → return → notice → unpaid; statutory conditions apply

beats.say: हर return automatic crime नहीं; पूरी statutory conditions जाँचनी होंगी।
beats.on_screen: Return alone ≠ automatic offence

beats.say: क्रम देखो: रकम कम, return, notice, फिर भी unpaid, फिर कानूनी शर्तों की जाँच।
beats.on_screen: Funds short → return → notice → unpaid → statutory conditions

beats.say: Section 138 में return अकेला पूरा legal test नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Return alone ≠ complete legal test

beats.say: Fee भेजने से पहले bank को ₹5,000 दो तो? Charges छोड़कर funding ₹0 से ₹5,000 हुई; फिर institution के लिए instrument निकला।
beats.on_screen: Fund first → issue fee instrument

beats.say: अपने ₹10,000, supplier को ₹15,000 चाहिए तो? Approved facility ने extra ₹5,000 दिए; borrowing ₹0 से ₹5,000 हुई।
beats.on_screen: Own ₹10,000 + approved credit ₹5,000

beats.say: पहला Demand Draft है: secure transfer का bank-issued prepaid instrument। Recharge जैसे पहले पैसे; ordinary cheque में बाद में account से payment माँगते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Demand draft: prepaid, bank-issued

beats.say: दूसरा Overdraft है: short-term credit से अपने balance से ज्यादा निकालना। Supplier के extra ₹5,000 लौटाने होंगे, savings नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Temporary gap → borrowed excess → repayment obligation

beats.say: Draft borrowing नहीं; खाली account OD permission नहीं। Approved credit चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Prepaid ≠ credit; OD requires approval

beats.say: Fee draft में advance funding; temporary business gap में OD borrowing।
beats.on_screen: Prepaid fee transfer / short-term business credit

beats.say: Recipient बाद के balance पर क्यों निर्भर नहीं? Customer ने पहले ₹3,000 दिए; backing ₹0 से ₹3,000 हुई, फिर draft निकला।
beats.on_screen: Receive ₹3,000 → issue ₹3,000 draft

beats.say: इसी prepayment से bank guarantee आती है: bank के पास payment की backing पहले पहुँच चुकी है।
beats.on_screen: Cause: funds already received

beats.say: इसलिए customer के later balance से draft funding जुटाने की जरूरत नहीं।
beats.on_screen: No reliance on later customer balance for draft funding

beats.say: Backing ₹3,000, draft ₹3,000: दोनों रकम मिलाकर जाँचो।
beats.on_screen: Received ₹3,000 matches draft ₹3,000

beats.say: यह funding assurance है, हर payment problem मिटने की guarantee नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Funding assurance ≠ immunity from every problem

beats.say: Guarantee की वजह याद रखो: पहले मिली रकम।
beats.on_screen: Advance funding → bank guarantee

beats.say: अपने ₹10,000 और OD Limit ₹40,000 हो तो कितना उपलब्ध? चित्र own funds और credit अलग करके जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: OD illustration: own funds plus credit

beats.say: बाएँ ₹10,000 अपने; दाएँ ₹40,000 borrowing ceiling। अलग डिब्बों जैसे समझो; arrow अपने पैसे को loan नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Separate boxes: own ₹10,000 / approved credit up to ₹40,000

beats.say: कुल ₹10,000 plus ₹40,000, यानी up to ₹50,000। Maximum है, निकालना जरूरी नहीं; interest केवल इस्तेमाल हुई OD पर।
beats.on_screen: Maximum ₹50,000; interest on used credit only

beats.say: ₹25,000 निकाले: ₹10,000 अपने, ₹15,000 borrowed। Interest principal ₹15,000 है; calculation के लिए rate और समय भी चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Shade only ₹15,000 used OD

beats.say: Availability और debt अलग हैं; यह ₹40,000 limit सबका हक नहीं।
beats.on_screen: ₹10,000 + ₹40,000 = ₹50,000 availability; only used OD is debt; illustrative limit

beats.say: Jan Dhan account से automatic OD? Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana में eligible account holders को facility मिल सकती है।
beats.on_screen: PMJDY → eligible holders → possible OD

beats.say: 'Eligible', 'may receive': शर्तें पूरी हों तो credit मिल सकता है; account खुलना borrowing की मंजूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Account access ≠ automatic credit eligibility

beats.say: Exam में 'हर holder को automatic OD' से बचो; access conditional है।
beats.on_screen: Conditional, not automatic

beats.say: Cheque का machine-readable code कैसा? MICR, Magnetic Ink Character Recognition: 9 digits, Iron Oxide ink, automated clearance के लिए।
beats.on_screen: MICR: 9 digits; magnetic ink; cheque clearance

beats.say: ₹2,000 transfer किस branch को जाए? सही 11-character code और account details भरे; identified destination branches 0 से 1 हुईं।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative transfer: unidentified branch → one identified branch

beats.say: यह Indian Financial System Code, IFSC है: electronic payment systems में participating bank branch का unique 11-character alphanumeric code। यानी letters और numbers वाला branch address, 11 digits नहीं।
beats.on_screen: IFSC: unique branch identifier; 11 alphanumeric characters

beats.say: Branch और account अलग हैं, जैसे building का पता और कमरे का नंबर।
beats.on_screen: Branch identifier ≠ account number

beats.say: Form में IFSC branch पहचानता है, account नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Apply IFSC: electronic destination branch

beats.say: 100 cheques कैसे पढ़ोगे? मान लो machine processing से pending batch 100 से 0 हुआ; speed का दावा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative pending batch: 100 → 0; no measured speed

beats.say: यह MICR-enabled processing है। Ink की magnetic properties से suitable machine characters पहचानती है; ink सजावट नहीं, पढ़ने में मदद है।
beats.on_screen: Magnetic properties → character recognition

beats.say: जैसे files अलग खानों में रखो, machine cheques sort करती है। Manual reading घटती है, processing जल्दी और accurate होती है।
beats.on_screen: Readable characters → consistent sorting → faster, accurate processing

beats.say: Pending 100 से 0: यह completed batch है, measured speed नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative completion, not a speed benchmark

beats.say: बेहतर accuracy का मतलब zero errors या fixed speed नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Improvement ≠ error-free processing or fixed speed

beats.say: MICR की chain है: readable characters से sorting और processing आसान।
beats.on_screen: Recognition → sorting → processing

beats.say: Electronic transfer में branch routing के लिए IFSC NEFT, RTGS और account-number-based IMPS में इस्तेमाल होता है। IMPS, यानी Immediate Payment Service, तुरंत transfer देता है; इसके दूसरे addressing modes भी हैं।
beats.on_screen: IFSC uses: NEFT / RTGS / account-based IMPS; alternative IMPS addressing exists

beats.say: साथ देखो: MICR के 9 digits, magnetic ink से cheque clearance; IFSC के 11 alphanumeric characters से electronic branch पहचान। Account number अलग है।
beats.on_screen: MICR: 9 digits, cheque processing | IFSC: 11 characters, branch routing

beats.say: ये code lengths हैं, speeds नहीं: NEFT batches, RTGS individual settlement, IMPS instant transfer देता है।
beats.on_screen: Code format versus payment mechanism

beats.say: Exam में format से function मिलाओ; सही branch के साथ सही beneficiary account भी चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Match code and function; correct branch + correct account

beats.say: अब शुरुआत का जवाब: cheque देना instruction है; successful payment अलग stage है। Payment समझते समय पैसा, order, funding और destination—ये 4 चीजें अलग जाँचो।
beats.on_screen: Final checklist: money / instruction / funding / destination

notes.about: This unit distinguishes deposit money from payment instructions, explains negotiable instruments and their parties, and connects demand drafts, overdrafts and banking codes to their functions.
key_questions: Who promises, orders, pays and receives payment in each instrument?
When does a cheque instruction become payment, and when can dishonour have criminal consequences?
How do advance funding, approved credit and used borrowing differ?
How do MICR and IFSC serve different banking tasks?

problems.problem: MICR is named and its format supplied before the required numerical cheque-processing example runs. The learner first receives a code-and-expansion list rather than seeing the processing need and mechanism.
problems.fix: Run the 100-cheque example first, including suitable equipment reading the special ink and sorting the cheques; then name MICR, expand it and establish its nine-digit format. Fund this reordering and opening by cutting the repeated batch-completion explanation in b65.

problems.problem: Several consecutive beats repeat an already completed explanation: the dishonour sequence and automatic-crime warning, IFSC not identifying an account, and batch completion not measuring speed. These are duplicate recaps rather than new teaching.
problems.fix: Keep one dishonour flow with its statutory-condition warning, one branch-versus-account boundary test, and one MICR chain recap. Remove the duplicate statements in b35–b36, b61 and b65 as appropriate, using the saved space for required openings.

problems.problem: The payment-channel classification names all five routes but does not teach them through consistent comparison slots. UPI and debit cards receive only brief operational fragments, while NEFT and RTGS receive settlement criteria. The basis and differences are therefore uneven despite the part claiming a complete classification.
problems.fix: Use a compact common comparison for every channel: what the customer uses, how it instructs movement of the same deposit, and a familiar place of use. Retain the NEFT–RTGS settlement contrast as their specific distinction. Pay for this by merging the repeated instrument comparisons in b22–b25 with the examples already taught in b6–b12.

problems.problem: The maker's notes primarily describe a patch history rather than explaining this unit's place in the chapter and its substantive teaching decisions.
problems.fix: Describe the unit's role between currency topics and the payment ecosystem, and record decisions about promise versus order, funding versus credit, and code function.

replace_beats.say: दुकान पर QR scan करके app में payment मंजूर करते हो: UPI, Unified Payments Interface, उसी deposit को तुरंत दूसरे account तक पहुँचाता है। Debit card दुकान की machine पर इस्तेमाल करते हो; उसकी authorisation से linked account के deposit से payment होती है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Common slots: customer uses → authorises deposit movement → familiar place. UPI: app + QR → account payment → kirana. Debit card: card + terminal → linked-account payment → shop.

replace_beats.say: Supplier के लिए cheque लिखते हो; collection पर bank से deposit payment माँगी जाती है। Rent के लिए NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer, में beneficiary details देकर transfer instruction देते हो; settlement batches में होता है। बड़ी purchase में RTGS, Real Time Gross Settlement, की instruction देते हो; हर transfer अलग, पूरी रकम का real-time settlement होता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Cheque: written order → collection and payment → supplier. NEFT: beneficiary instruction → batch settlement → rent. RTGS: beneficiary instruction → individual real-time gross settlement → large purchase. All move account deposits.

replace_beats.say: Written documents में Rahul वाला अपना promise, Promissory Note है; retailer को ₹1 लाख 90 days बाद देने का order, Bill of Exchange है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Business-credit documents: own written promise / written order to another party.

replace_beats.say: Cheque उसी order की bank वाली शाखा है: customer लिखता है, bank को payment करने को कहता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Customer writes → bank is instructed → payee receives after successful processing.

replace_beats.say: Note में अपनी commitment, bill में दूसरे को order, cheque में bank को order है; UPI इस legal family का चौथा member नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Promise / order / bank-addressed order. Customer issues cheque; bank receives order. Channels are a separate grouping.

replace_beats.say: याद रखो: 'मैं दूँगा, तुम दो, bank दे'; channel बदला, deposit money नहीं।

replace_beats.say: रकम कम होने से unpaid return, यानी dishonour हुआ; notice के बाद भी रकम न मिले तो Section 138 में criminal liability का सवाल आता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Insufficient funds → unpaid return → statutory demand notice → continued non-payment; applicable statutory conditions required.

replace_beats.say: लेकिन return अकेला crime साबित नहीं करता; statutory conditions पूरी होनी चाहिए।

replace_beats.say: याद रखो: legal consequence के लिए पूरा क्रम जाँचो।

replace_beats.say: एक branch में तुम्हारे और पड़ोसी के accounts हों तो IFSC एक, account numbers अलग होंगे।
replace_beats.on_screen: Boundary test: one branch identifier, two distinct account identifiers.

replace_beats.say: Transfer form में दोनों पहचानें मिलाकर destination भरो।
replace_beats.on_screen: Apply the definition: IFSC identifies the participating branch; account details identify the beneficiary account.

replace_beats.say: Bank में 100 cheques का ढेर हो तो हर code हाथ से पढ़ोगे? मान लो suitable equipment ने पूरा batch process किया; पढ़ने के लिए बाकी cheques 100 से 0 हुए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Hypothetical cheque-processing centre: 100 pending cheques → completed batch → 0 pending. No elapsed time or speed measurement.

replace_beats.say: कैसे? Equipment ने खास ink के magnetic properties से printed characters पहचाने और cheques sort किए; staff को हर character दोबारा हाथ से नहीं पढ़ना पड़ा।
replace_beats.on_screen: Replay mechanism: special magnetic ink → suitable reader recognises characters → equipment sorts cheques.

replace_beats.say: इस machine reading से cheques जल्दी और accurately process होते हैं, जैसे files पहचानकर सही खानों में रखना।
replace_beats.on_screen: Recognised characters → consistent sorting → quick, accurate processing.

replace_beats.say: इस example में पढ़ी गई batch ही mechanism दिखाती है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Evidence within the illustration: recognised characters enabled sorting of the batch; no empirical benchmark claimed.

replace_beats.say: बेहतर accuracy का मतलब error-free processing नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Limit: improved accuracy is not a guarantee of zero errors.

replace_beats.say: Chain याद रखो: ink से पहचान, फिर sorting, फिर processing।
replace_beats.on_screen: MICR chain recap: magnetic-ink recognition → sorting → processing.

beat.say: इसी पहचान को MICR, Magnetic Ink Character Recognition, कहते हैं। Cheque clearance के लिए इसका code 9 digits का, Iron Oxide ink में लिखा होता है; अभी देखी machine reading इसका काम समझाती है।
